findings: The selected digital Arabic includes full chains of transmission; the working English retains them.

The Brill print abbreviates the first narrator to al-Humaydi while the selected digital text and Darussalam give his name. Honorific wording and orthography also differ. These are recorded as witness differences, not silently harmonized.

The first two narration bodies were visually compared against the Darussalam Arabic and the older print. No additional substantive body clause was identified in those comparisons. This is an AI review, not an independent human audit.
The sample and a digital edition are not presumed identical merely because their translator is the same.
A close translation still involves linguistic judgment; zero interpretation and infallibility cannot honestly be promised.
Entries 3–7 have AI comparison records and declared wording choices; no human accuracy certification is claimed. The derived Hadith 5 correction does not modify the pinned digital input.

arabic_blocks: [59] حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال: حدثنا فليح ح وحدثني إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا محمد بن فليح قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثني هلال بن علي عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة قال:

Some of the people said: “He heard what he said and disliked what he said.” Others said: “Rather, he did not hear.” When he finished speaking, he said: “Where—I think—is the one who asked about the Hour?” He said: “Here I am, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When the trust is lost, await the Hour.” He said: “How is it lost?” He said: “When authority is entrusted to those unfit for it, await the Hour.”

arabic_blocks: [63] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث عن سعيد هو المقبري عن شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يقول:

بينما نحن جلوس مع النبي ﷺ في المسجد دخل رجل على جمل فأناخه في المسجد ثم عقله، ثم قال لهم أيكم محمد والنبي ﷺ متكئ بين ظهرانيهم فقلنا هذا الرجل الأبيض المتكئ، فقال له الرجل بن عبد المطلب، فقال له النبي ﷺ قد أجبتك، فقال الرجل للنبي ﷺ إني سائلك فمشدد عليك في المسألة فلا تجد علي في نفسك، فقال سل عما بدا لك، فقال أسألك بربك ورب من قبلك آلله أرسلك إلى الناس كلهم، فقال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصلي الصلوات الخمس في اليوم والليلة قال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصوم هذا الشهر من السنة قال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن تأخذ هذه الصدقة من أغنيائنا فتقسمها على فقرائنا، فقال النبي ﷺ اللهم نعم، فقال الرجل آمنت بما جئت به وأنا رسول من ورائي من قومي وأنا ضِمام بن ثعلبة أخو بني سعد بن بكر
رواه موسى وعلي بن عبد الحميد عن سليمان عن ثابت عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ بهذا.
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id—he is al-Maqburi—from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, that he heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

While we were sitting with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, a man entered on a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque and then hobbled it. Then he said to them: “Which of you is Muhammad?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was reclining among them. We said: “This fair-skinned man who is reclining.” The man said to him: “Son of ‘Abd al-Muttalib!” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “I have answered you.” The man said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “I am going to question you and be insistent in questioning you, so do not feel anger toward me.” He said: “Ask whatever occurs to you.” He said: “I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: did Allah send you to all people?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should perform the five prayers in the day and night?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should fast this month of the year?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you to take this charity from our rich and distribute it among our poor?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Allah, yes.” The man said: “I believe in what you have brought. I am a messenger from those of my people whom I have left behind. I am Dimam ibn Tha‘labah, a member of Banu Sa‘d ibn Bakr.”
Musa and ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid transmitted this report from Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

When he read it, he tore it up. I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed against them that they should be utterly torn apart.

Ibn ‘Abbas said: “He was Khidr.” Ubayy ibn Ka‘b passed by them, and Ibn ‘Abbas called him and said: “This companion of mine and I have disputed about Musa’s companion, whom Musa asked how to meet. Musa’s young companion said to him: {Did you see? When we took shelter at the rock, I forgot the fish; none but Satan made me forget to mention it.} {He said: That is what we were seeking. So they retraced their steps.} They found Khidr, and what happened between them was what Allah, mighty and majestic, recounted in His Book.”

مثل ما بعثني الله به من الهدى والعلم كمثل الغيث الكثير أصاب أرضا فكان منها نقية قبلت الماء فأنبتت الكلأ والعشب الكثير وكانت منها أجادب أمسكت الماء فنفع الله بها الناس فشربوا وسقوا وزرعوا وأصابت منها طائفة أخرى إنما هي قيعان لا تمسك ماء ولا تنبت كلأ فذلك مثل من فقه في دين الله ونفعه ما بعثني الله به فعلم وعلم ومثل من لم يرفع بذلك رأسا ولم يقبل هدى الله الذي أرسلت به قال أبو عبد الله قال إسحاق وكان منها طائفة قيّلت الماء قاع يعلوه الماء والصفصف المستوي من الأرض
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The guidance and knowledge with which Allah sent me are like abundant rain falling on land. Some of it was good ground that accepted the water and brought forth plentiful pasture and fresh grass. Some of it was hard ground that held the water, through which Allah benefited people: they drank, watered and cultivated. It fell on another tract that was only level ground, neither holding water nor growing pasture. This is the likeness of one who gains understanding of Allah’s religion and benefits from what Allah sent me with, learning and teaching; and the likeness of one who pays it no heed and does not accept Allah’s guidance with which I was sent.”
